[Mandatory] Summary:
 A buffer over-read vulnerability exists in the `name_len` function within `smbutil.c`. The issue is triggered when parsing a specially crafted SMB/CIFS packet, where the length field in the name string can cause the processing pointer to advance past the end of the captured buffer. This leads to an out-of-bounds read of one byte when the loop continues, as seen in the code where the pointer `s` is incremented without a subsequent bounds check before the next access.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
 Missing bounds check after advancing a pointer based on untrusted data from the packet.
[Mandatory] Attack Surface:
Network packet analyzer (tcpdump) processing SMB/CIFS traffic
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Denial of Service / Information Disclosure
[Optional] Trigger / Attack vector:
 Crafted SMB/CIFS packet
[Mandatory] Key code/struct excerpt (minimal):
```c
    while (*s) {
	if (s >= maxbuf)
	    return(-1);	/* name goes past the end of the buffer */
	ND_TCHECK2(*s, 1);
	s += (*s) + 1;
    }
```
Exploit:

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
Network packet capture (pcap file) or live network interface

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Relative out-of-bounds read (1 byte)

[Mandatory] Exploitability summary (1 sentence):
An attacker can control the offset to read a single byte from memory adjacent to the packet buffer, potentially leading to information disclosure.

[Mandatory] Exploit script (summary, 3—6 bullets):
- Craft an SMB/CIFS packet containing a name string.
- Set the length byte within the name string to a value that, when added to the current pointer, places it just before the end of the packet buffer.
- Ensure the subsequent byte (which would be read in the next loop iteration) is not part of the actual captured packet.
- The `name_len` function will increment its pointer past the buffer and then attempt to read one byte out of bounds in the next loop iteration.
- Supplying this packet to tcpdump (either via a live capture or a pcap file) will trigger the vulnerability.

Fix
[Mandatory] Fix code:
```c
    while (*s) {
	if (s >= maxbuf)
	    return(-1);	/* name goes past the end of the buffer */
	ND_TCHECK2(*s, 1);
	s += (*s) + 1;
	ND_TCHECK2(*s, 1);
    }
```

[Mandatory] Fix summary:
 The patch adds a bounds check (`ND_TCHECK2(*s, 1);`) immediately after the pointer `s` is advanced within the parsing loop. This ensures that the newly pointed-to location is still within the captured buffer before it is accessed.

[Mandatory] Summary:
 The vulnerability exists in the `lookup_bytestring` function within `addrtoname.c`. It is triggered when searching for a byte string in a hash table where an existing entry is shorter than the input string. The code is exploitable because the `memcmp` call uses the length of the input string to compare against the stored string, leading to an out-of-bounds read past the end of the stored string's buffer.

 The `memcmp` call in the hash table search loop does not check if the input string length (`nlen`) is equal to the stored string's length (`tp->bs_nbytes`) before performing the comparison.

Network packet analyzer (tcpdump)

Information Disclosure

 Crafted network packet / pcap file

```c
	while (tp->bs_nxt)
		if (tp->bs_addr0 == i &&
		    tp->bs_addr1 == j &&
		    tp->bs_addr2 == k &&
		    memcmp((const char *)bs, (const char *)(tp->bs_bytes), nlen) == 0)
			return tp;
		else
			tp = tp->bs_nxt;
```
Exploit:

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
Crafted network packet / pcap file

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Out-of-bounds read

The vulnerability is easily triggered by processing a specially crafted packet that causes a hash collision with a shorter, pre-existing string in the table.

- Craft a network packet containing a byte string.
- Ensure the packet causes tcpdump to call `lookup_bytestring` with this string.
- The crafted string must hash to the same bucket as a shorter string already present in the `bytestringtable`.
- When `lookup_bytestring` iterates through the bucket, it will compare the long crafted string against the short stored string.
- The `memcmp` will read past the end of the short string's buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read.

Fix
[Mandatory] Fix code:
```c
	while (tp->bs_nxt)
		if (nlen == tp->bs_nbytes &&
		    tp->bs_addr0 == i &&
		    tp->bs_addr1 == j &&
		    tp->bs_addr2 == k &&
		    memcmp((const char *)bs, (const char *)(tp->bs_bytes), nlen) == 0)
			return tp;
```

[Mandatory] Fix summary:
 The fix adds a length check (`nlen == tp->bs_nbytes`) to the conditional statement inside the hash table search loop. This ensures that `memcmp` is only called when the input string and the stored string have the same length, preventing the out-of-bounds read.

The Vulnerability
[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
[Mandatory] Summary:
The vulnerability exists in the `arp_print` function within `print-arp.c`. When processing an ARP packet, the code could read past the end of the captured packet buffer if the protocol address length field (`PROTO_LEN(ap)`) was larger than the available data. This occurs because the check `ND_TTEST2(*TPA(ap), PROTO_LEN(ap))` is intended to validate that `PROTO_LEN(ap)` bytes are available from the `TPA(ap)` pointer, but the subsequent handling of protocol addresses does not consistently respect this boundary, leading to an out-of-bounds read.

Insufficient validation of the protocol address length field before reading memory.
[Mandatory] Attack Surface:
Network packet capture analysis (e.g., tcpdump)
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Denial of Service (application crash) or potential information leak.
[Optional] Trigger / Attack vector:
A specially crafted ARP packet processed by the vulnerable tcpdump version.
[Mandatory] Key code/struct excerpt (minimal):
```c
	if (!ND_TTEST2(*TPA(ap), PROTO_LEN(ap))) {
		ND_PRINT((ndo, "%s", tstr));
		ND_DEFAULTPRINT((const u_char *)ap, length);
		return;
	}
```

Exploit:

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
Network packet capture (pcap file) containing a malicious ARP packet.

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Out-of-bounds read.

- Modify the ARP packet's header to set a large protocol address length.
- Ensure the actual packet data is smaller than the specified length.

[Mandatory] Fix code:
```c
	if (!ND_TTEST2(*TPA(ap), PROTO_LEN(ap))) {
		ND_PRINT((ndo, "%s", tstr));
		ND_DEFAULTPRINT((const u_char *)ap, length);
		return;
	}
```

This is reflected in the diff by replacing direct `ipaddr_string` calls with `tpaddr_print_ip`/`spaddr_print_ip` which contain the necessary checks. The fix changes the ARP printer to only attempt to print protocol addresses as IPv4 when the protocol type is ETHERTYPE_IP/ETHERTYPE_TRAIL and the length is 4. For other cases, it uses functions that properly handle the specified length without assuming IPv4, preventing the out-of-bounds read.

The Vulnerability
[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:
CWE-125
[Mandatory] Summary:
The vulnerability exists in the `mp_capable_print` function within `print-mptcp.c`. An incorrect precedence in a length and flag check allows a packet with `opt_len` equal to 12 and `flags` not containing `TH_SYN` to pass validation. The code then proceeds to read 8 bytes from `mpc->sender_key` without sufficient bounds checking, leading to an out-of-bounds read.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
Incorrect operator precedence in a conditional check, where bitwise AND (`&`) was evaluated before the logical AND (`&&`).

Network packet parser (tcpdump)

static int
mp_capable_print(netdissect_options *ndo,
                 const u_char *opt, u_int opt_len, u_char flags)
{
        const struct mp_capable *mpc = (const struct mp_capable *) opt;

        if (!(opt_len == 12 && flags & TH_SYN) &&
            !(opt_len == 20 && (flags & (TH_SYN | TH_ACK)) == TH_ACK))
                return 0;

        if (MP_CAPABLE_OPT_VERSION(mpc->sub_ver) != 0) {
                ND_PRINT((ndo, " Unknown Version (%d)", MP_CAPABLE_OPT_VERSION(mpc->sub_ver)));
                return 1;
        }

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
Malformed network packet captured by tcpdump

Out-of-bounds read

[Mandatory] Exploit script (summary, 3—6 bullets):
- Craft an MPTCP packet with `opt_len` set to 12 and the `TH_SYN` flag unset in the TCP header.
- This packet will pass the first part of the conditional check: `!(opt_len == 12 && flags & TH_SYN)` evaluates to `!(1 && 0)` which is `!0` (true).
- The second part of the conditional check will also evaluate to true, allowing the function to continue.
- The function then calls `EXTRACT_64BITS(mpc->sender_key)`, reading 8 bytes from a potentially invalid memory location.
- Run `tcpdump` to capture this packet, causing the out-of-bounds read.

Fix
[Mandatory] Fix code:
static int
mp_capable_print(netdissect_options *ndo,
                 const u_char *opt, u_int opt_len, u_char flags)
{
        const struct mp_capable *mpc = (const struct mp_capable *) opt;

        if (!(opt_len == 12 && (flags & TH_SYN)) &&
            !(opt_len == 20 && (flags & (TH_SYN | TH_ACK)) == TH_ACK))
                return 0;

        if (MP_CAPABLE_OPT_VERSION(mpc->sub_ver) != 0) {
                ND_PRINT((ndo, " Unknown Version (%d)", MP_CAPABLE_OPT_VERSION(mpc->sub_ver)));
                return 1;
        }
[Mandatory] Fix summary:
The fix adds parentheses around the flag check `(flags & TH_SYN)` to ensure the bitwise AND operation is evaluated before the logical AND, correcting the validation logic.

The vulnerability exists in the `decode_rt_routing_info` function within `print-bgp.c`. It is triggered when processing a crafted BGP VPN packet where the function attempts to read the "origin AS" field and the "route target" field without sufficient bounds checks. This leads to an out-of-bounds read from the packet buffer (`pptr`), potentially leaking memory contents or causing a crash.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
The function reads from the packet buffer at offsets `pptr + 1` and `pptr[5]` without verifying that enough data remains, leading to a buffer over-read.

Network service (BGP parser in tcpdump)

```c
	ND_TCHECK_32BITS(pptr + 1);
	as_printf(ndo, asbuf, sizeof(asbuf), EXTRACT_32BITS(pptr + 1));

        plen-=32; /* adjust prefix length */

	if (64 < plen)
		return -1;

	memset(&route_target, 0, sizeof(route_target));
	ND_TCHECK2(pptr[5], (plen + 7) / 8);
	memcpy(&route_target, &pptr[5], (plen + 7) / 8);
```

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
Network packet capture processed by tcpdump

Out-of-bounds read

The exploit is easy to trigger by sending a specifically malformed BGP packet to a machine running tcpdump, leading to a predictable over-read.

- Ensure the packet data is shorter than the expected size for the "origin AS" and "route target" fields.

- tcpdump will call `decode_rt_routing_info`, which will read past the end of the provided packet buffer.
- This results in a crash or information disclosure.

Fix
[Mandatory] Fix code:
```c
	/* With at least "origin AS", possibly with "route target". */
	ND_TCHECK_32BITS(pptr + 1);
	as_printf(ndo, asbuf, sizeof(asbuf), EXTRACT_32BITS(pptr + 1));

        plen-=32; /* adjust prefix length */

	if (64 < plen)
		return -1;

	/* From now on (plen + 7) / 8 evaluates to { 0, 1, 2, ..., 8 }
	 * and gives the number of octets in the variable-length "route
	 * target" field inside this NLRI "prefix". Look for it.
	 */
	memset(&route_target, 0, sizeof(route_target));
	ND_TCHECK2(pptr[5], (plen + 7) / 8);
	memcpy(&route_target, &pptr[5], (plen + 7) / 8);
```

The patch adds a `ND_TCHECK_32BITS` macro call before reading the 4-byte "origin AS" field and corrects the offset for reading the variable-length "route target" field from `pptr[1]` to `pptr[5]`.

commit_message:
CVE-2017-13053/BGP: fix VPN route target bounds checks

decode_rt_routing_info() didn't check bounds before fetching 4 octets of
the origin AS field and could over-read the input buffer, put it right.

It also fetched the varying number of octets of the route target field
from 4 octets lower than the correct offset, put it right.

It also used the same temporary buffer explicitly through as_printf()
and implicitly through bgp_vpn_rd_print() so the end result of snprintf()
was not what was originally intended.

[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
[Mandatory] Summary:
The bug is in the `sfe_copy_data_fp` function in `programs/common.c`. It is triggered when processing a sound file where the calculated maximum signal value (`max`) is zero, subnormal, infinite, or NaN. The function then performs a division operation (`data [k] /= max`) without validating `max` first, leading to a potential divide-by-zero or generation of infinite/NaN values, which can be interpreted as an out-of-bounds read vulnerability by subsequent memory operations.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
Unchecked `max` variable used as a divisor without validation.
[Mandatory] Attack Surface:
Local file processing (libsndfile library).
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Denial of Service via application crash.
[Optional] Trigger / Attack vector:
Malformed audio file processed by an application using libsndfile.
[Mandatory] Key code/struct excerpt (minimal):
```c
sf_command (infile, SFC_CALC_SIGNAL_MAX, &max, sizeof (max)) ;
if (!normalize && max < 1.0)
{ /* ... */ }
else
{ /* ... */
    for (k = 0 ; k < readcount * channels ; k++)
    {   data [k] /= max;
        if (!isfinite (data [k])) /* infinite or NaN */
            return 1;
    }
    /* ... */
}
```
Exploit:

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
File parsing via libsndfile.

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Denial of service (crash).

- Create a malicious audio file with a channel that forces the maximum signal value to be zero.
- Load the file using an application linked against the vulnerable libsndfile version.
- The application calls `sfe_copy_data_fp`, which divides by zero.
- The generated infinite or NaN value propagates, causing the program to crash.
- No further memory corruption or code execution is achieved.

Fix
[Mandatory] Fix code:
```c
sf_command (infile, SFC_CALC_SIGNAL_MAX, &max, sizeof (max)) ;
if (!isnormal (max)) /* neither zero, subnormal, infinite, nor NaN */
    return 1 ;

if (!normalize && max < 1.0)
{ /* ... */ }
else
{ /* ... */
    for (k = 0 ; k < readcount * channels ; k++)
    {   data [k] /= max;

        if (!isfinite (data [k])) /* infinite or NaN */
            return 1;
    }
    /* ... */
```

commit_message:
x86: Guard against corrupted PLT

There should be only one entry in PLT for a given symbol.  Set howto to
NULL after processing a PLT entry to guard against corrupted PLT so that
the duplicated PLT entries are skipped.

	PR binutils/22170
	 * elf32-i386.c (elf_i386_get_synthetic_symtab): Guard against
	 corrupted PLT.
	 * elf64-x86-64.c (elf_x86_64_get_synthetic_symtab): Likewise.

commit_message:
kvm_set_irq() has an internal buffer of three irq routing entries, allowing
connecting a GSI to three IRQ chips or on MSI.  However setup_routing_entry()
does not properly enforce this, allowing three irqchip routes followed by
an MSI route to overflow the buffer.

Fix by ensuring that an MSI entry is added to an empty list.

commit_message:
mm: thp: fix pmd_present for split_huge_page and PROT_NONE with THP

In many places !pmd_present has been converted to pmd_none.  For pmds
that's equivalent and pmd_none is quicker so using pmd_none is better.

However (unless we delete pmd_present) we should provide an accurate
pmd_present too.  This will avoid the risk of code thinking the pmd is non
present because it's under __split_huge_page_map, see the pmd_mknotpresent
there and the comment above it.

If the page has been mprotected as PROT_NONE, it would also lead to a
pmd_present false negative in the same way as the race with
split_huge_page.

Because the PSE bit stays on at all times (both during split_huge_page and
when the _PAGE_PROTNONE bit get set), we could only check for the PSE bit,
but checking the PROTNONE bit too is still good to remember pmd_present
must always keep PROT_NONE into account.

This explains a not reproducible BUG_ON that was seldom reported on the
lists.

The same issue is in pmd_large, it would go wrong with both PROT_NONE and
if it races with split_huge_page.

[Optional] Disclosure / Patch Dates:

[Optional] Affected products/versions:

The Vulnerability
[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:
Incorrect pmd_present check leads to false negatives
[Mandatory] Summary:
The `pmd_present` function in `arch/x86/include/asm/pgtable.h` incorrectly checks for the presence of a PMD entry by only testing the `_PAGE_PRESENT` flag. This logic can lead to false negatives when a transparent huge page is being split or when a page is protected with `PROT_NONE`, causing the kernel to incorrectly believe a page is not present. The flawed check is `return pmd_flags(pmd) & _PAGE_PRESENT;`, which fails to account for other valid states of a PMD entry.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
The `pmd_present` function's check was incomplete, only considering `_PAGE_PRESENT` and not other valid flags like `_PAGE_PSE` and `_PAGE_PROTNONE`.
[Mandatory] Attack Surface:
Kernel memory management subsystem (transparent huge pages)
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Kernel panic / Denial of Service (DoS)
[Optional] Trigger / Attack vector:
Race with `split_huge_page` or memory protected with `mprotect(PROT_NONE)` on transparent huge pages.
[Mandatory] Key code/struct excerpt (minimal):
static inline int pmd_present(pmd_t pmd)
{
	return pmd_flags(pmd) & _PAGE_PRESENT;
}
Exploit:

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
Race with `split_huge_page` or memory protected with `mprotect(PROT_NONE)` on transparent huge pages.

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Kernel panic (BUG_ON trigger)

[Mandatory] Exploitability summary (1 sentence):
Reliability may be low due to race condition dependency, but a successful trigger results in a kernel crash.

[Mandatory] Exploit script (summary, 3—6 bullets):
- Target a system using Transparent Huge Pages (THP).
- Trigger a memory management operation that calls `pmd_present`.
- Simultaneously, initiate a race condition by calling `split_huge_page` on the same memory region.
- Alternatively, use `mprotect` to set a THP region to `PROT_NONE`.
- The race or state change causes `pmd_present` to return false when it should be true.
- This incorrect state eventually leads to a `BUG_ON` assertion failure, crashing the kernel.

Fix
[Mandatory] Fix code:
static inline int pmd_present(pmd_t pmd)
{
	/*
	 * Checking for _PAGE_PSE is needed too because
	 * split_huge_page will temporarily clear the present bit (but
	 * the _PAGE_PSE flag will remain set at all times while the

commit_message:
mm: thp: fix pmd_present for split_huge_page and PROT_NONE with THP

In many places !pmd_present has been converted to pmd_none.  For pmds
that's equivalent and pmd_none is quicker so using pmd_none is better.

However (unless we delete pmd_present) we should provide an accurate
pmd_present too.  This will avoid the risk of code thinking the pmd is non
present because it's under __split_huge_page_map, see the pmd_mknotpresent
there and the comment above it.

If the page has been mprotected as PROT_NONE, it would also lead to a
pmd_present false negative in the same way as the race with
split_huge_page.

Because the PSE bit stays on at all times (both during split_huge_page and
when the _PAGE_PROTNONE bit get set), we could only check for the PSE bit,
but checking the PROTNONE bit too is still good to remember pmd_present
must always keep PROT_NONE into account.

This explains a not reproducible BUG_ON that was seldom reported on the
lists.

The same issue is in pmd_large, it would go wrong with both PROT_NONE and
if it races with split_huge_page.

commit_message:
printk: fix buffer overflow when calling log_prefix function from call_console_drivers

This patch corrects a buffer overflow in kernels from 3.0 to 3.4 when calling
log_prefix() function from call_console_drivers().

This bug existed in previous releases but has been revealed with commit
162a7e7500f9664636e649ba59defe541b7c2c60 (2.6.39 => 3.0) that made changes
about how to allocate memory for early printk buffer (use of memblock_alloc).
It disappears with commit 7ff9554bb578ba02166071d2d487b7fc7d860d62 (3.4 => 3.5)
that does a refactoring of printk buffer management.

In log_prefix(), the access to "p[0]", "p[1]", "p[2]" or
"simple_strtoul(&p[1], &endp, 10)" may cause a buffer overflow as this
function is called from call_console_drivers by passing "&LOG_BUF(cur_index)"
where the index must be masked to do not exceed the buffer's boundary.

The trick is to prepare in call_console_drivers() a buffer with the necessary
data (PRI field of syslog message) to be safely evaluated in log_prefix().

This patch can be applied to stable kernel branches 3.0.y, 3.2.y and 3.4.y.

Without this patch, one can freeze a server running this loop from shell :
  $ export DUMMY=`cat /dev/urandom | tr -dc '12345AZERTYUIOPQSDFGHJKLMWXCVBNazertyuiopqsdfghjklmwxcvbn' | head -c255`
  $ while true do

commit_message:
NLS: improve UTF8 -> UTF16 string conversion routine

The utf8s_to_utf16s conversion routine needs to be improved.  Unlike
its utf16s_to_utf8s sibling, it doesn't accept arguments specifying
the maximum length of the output buffer or the endianness of its
16-bit output.

This patch (as1501) adds the two missing arguments, and adjusts the
only two places in the kernel where the function is called.  A
follow-on patch will add a third caller that does utilize the new
capabilities.

The two conversion routines are still annoyingly inconsistent in the
way they handle invalid byte combinations.  But that's a subject for a
different patch.

commit_message:
NLS: improve UTF8 -> UTF16 string conversion routine

The utf8s_to_utf16s conversion routine needs to be improved.  Unlike
its utf16s_to_utf8s sibling, it doesn't accept arguments specifying
the maximum length of the output buffer or the endianness of its
16-bit output.

This patch (as1501) adds the two missing arguments, and adjusts the
only two places in the kernel where the function is called.  A
follow-on patch will add a third caller that does utilize the new
capabilities.

The two conversion routines are still annoyingly inconsistent in the
way they handle invalid byte combinations.  But that's a subject for a
different patch.

CC: Clemens Ladisch <clemens@ladisch.de>

commit_message:
Fix a crash seen in ChromeFrame when opening a non CF top level tab from a CF page.

This was a regression caused by the fix for bug http://code.google.com/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=168308
which was to not invalidate the protocol sink mapping for CF pages which are switched in from IE.

The crash in this case occurs because the protocol sink mapping is removed in the call to IInternetProtocol::Terminate
as this is treated as a ChromeFrame request. This is only a temporary CF url which eventually transitions to
the actual URL which  is opened in IE. For the curious we intercept IInternetProtocol::LockRequest and for
the special gcf://attach_external_tab requests we addref the protocol data and return without calling the original
LockRequest API. When UnlockRequest is invoked we rely on the protocol data mapping to exist to release the
protocol data and return without calling the original UnlockRequest API.

In this case the sequence is IInternetProtocol::LockRequest, IInternetProtocolRoot::Terminate followed by
IInternetProtocol::UnlockRequest. In our terminate handler we remove the protocol data mapping for the attach tab
request. When UnlockRequest is called we call the original API and end up crashing.

Fix is to not invalidate the protocol data mapping for attach tab requests.

A test for this is in the works by robertshield.

R=robertshield

commit_message:
Fix invalid read in gdImageCreateFromTiffPtr()

tiff_invalid_read.tiff is corrupt, and causes an invalid read in
gdImageCreateFromTiffPtr(), but not in gdImageCreateFromTiff(). The culprit
is dynamicGetbuf(), which doesn't check for out-of-bound reads. In this case,
dynamicGetbuf() is called with a negative dp->pos, but also positive buffer
overflows have to be handled, in which case 0 has to be returned (cf. commit
75e29a9).

Fixing dynamicGetbuf() exhibits that the corrupt TIFF would still create
the image, because the return value of TIFFReadRGBAImage() is not checked.
We do that, and let createFromTiffRgba() fail if TIFFReadRGBAImage() fails.

This issue had been reported by Ibrahim El-Sayed to security@libgd.org.

commit_message:
specrec: better handle unexpected PS

Parametric Stereo (PS) can arrive at any moment in input files. PS
changes the number of output channels and therefore requires more
allocated memory in various structures from hDecoder.

The current faad2 code attempts to perform allocation surgery in
hDecoder to recover from this. This works well when there is only one
frame channel, else it creates large number of memory corruption
issues.

If there is more than one input channel, return cleanly with error
code. It would be nice to handle this, but this is likely to be a lot
of work and is beyond the scope of a security fix.

This commit addresses CVE-2018-20360 and CVE-2018-20199 (fixes #32,
fixes #24).

commit_message:
syntax.c: check for syntax element inconsistencies

Implicit channel mapping reconfiguration is explicitely forbidden by
ISO/IEC 13818-7:2006 (8.5.3.3). Decoders should be able to detect such
files and reject them. FAAD2 does not perform any kind of checks
regarding this.

This leads to security vulnerabilities when processing crafted AAC
files performing such reconfigurations.

Add checks to decode_sce_lfe and decode_cpe to make sure such
inconsistencies are detected as early as possible.

These checks first read hDecoder->frame: if this is not the first
frame then we make sure that the syntax element at the same position
in the previous frame also had element_id id_syn_ele. If not, return
21 as this is a fatal file structure issue.

This patch addresses CVE-2018-20362 (fixes #26) and possibly other
related issues.

commit_message:
sbr_hfadj: sanitize frequency band borders

user passed f_table_lim contains frequency band borders. Frequency
bands are groups of consecutive QMF channels. This means that their
bounds, as provided by f_table_lim, should never exceed MAX_M (maximum
number of QMF channels). c.f. ISO/IEC 14496-3:2001

FAAD2 does not verify this, leading to security issues when
processing files defining f_table_lim with values > MAX_M.

This patch sanitizes the values of f_table_lim so that they can be safely
used as index for Q_M_lim and G_lim arrays.

Fixes #21 (CVE-2018-20194).

commit_message:
KVM: x86: fix for buffer overflow in handling of MSR_KVM_SYSTEM_TIME (CVE-2013-1796)

If the guest sets the GPA of the time_page so that the request to update the
time straddles a page then KVM will write onto an incorrect page.  The
write is done byusing kmap atomic to get a pointer to the page for the time
structure and then performing a memcpy to that page starting at an offset
that the guest controls.  Well behaved guests always provide a 32-byte aligned
address, however a malicious guest could use this to corrupt host kernel
memory.

Tested: Tested against kvmclock unit test.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Honig <ahonig@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Marcelo Tosatti <mtosatti@redhat.com>

commit_message:
Drop packets forwarded via TCP if they are too big (CVE-2013-1428).

Normally all requests sent via the meta connections are checked so that they
cannot be larger than the input buffer. However, when packets are forwarded via
meta connections, they are copied into a packet buffer without checking whether
it fits into it. Since the packet buffer is allocated on the stack, this in
effect allows an authenticated remote node to cause a stack overflow.

This issue was found by Martin Schobert.

packet to the userspace buffer. Otherwise unrelated userspace memory might get
overridden by the kernel.

commit_message:
tg3: fix length overflow in VPD firmware parsing

Commit 184b89044fb6e2a74611dafa69b1dce0d98612c6 ("tg3: Use VPD fw version
when present") introduced VPD parsing that contained a potential length
overflow.

Limit the hardware's reported firmware string length (max 255 bytes) to
stay inside the driver's firmware string length (32 bytes). On overflow,
truncate the formatted firmware string instead of potentially overwriting
portions of the tg3 struct.

Remote iSCSI network packet

commit_message:
iscsi-target: fix heap buffer overflow on error

If a key was larger than 64 bytes, as checked by iscsi_check_key(), the
error response packet, generated by iscsi_add_notunderstood_response(),
would still attempt to copy the entire key into the packet, overflowing
the structure on the heap.

Remote preauthentication kernel memory corruption was possible if a
target was configured and listening on the network.

CVE-2013-2850

commit_message:
GFS2: rewrite fallocate code to write blocks directly

GFS2's fallocate code currently goes through the page cache. Since it's only
writing to the end of the file or to holes in it, it doesn't need to, and it
was causing issues on low memory environments. This patch pulls in some of
Steve's block allocation work, and uses it to simply allocate the blocks for
the file, and zero them out at allocation time.  It provides a slight
performance increase, and it dramatically simplifies the code.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Marzinski <bmarzins@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Steven Whitehouse <swhiteho@redhat.com>

```c
                return bytestream2_tell(&gb);

                *pd++ = bytestream2_get_byteu(&gb);
                *pd++ = bytestream2_get_byteu(&gb);
```

```cpp
    // depend may now no longer exist, or glyph positions may be wrong
    InlineTextBox* nextBox = nextTextBox();
    if (nextBox)
        nextBox->dirtyLineBoxes();
}
```

commit_message:
Clear SVGInlineTextBox fragments when the text changes.

This patch modifies SVGInlineTextBox::dirtyLineBoxes to clear all
following text boxes when invoked. Typically this method is called
when the underlying text string changes, and that change needs to
be propagated to all the boxes that use the text beyond the point
where the text is first modified.

When parsing deeply nested XML elements, the function unconditionally writes into the `parser->ltags` array at index `parser->level-1` without checking if the depth exceeds the array's bounds. This allows an attacker supplying a crafted XML document with excessive nesting to trigger an out-of-bounds write, corrupting memory and potentially leading to arbitrary code execution.

```c
			int atcnt = 0;

			MAKE_STD_ZVAL(tag);
			MAKE_STD_ZVAL(atr);

			array_init(tag);
			array_init(atr);

			_xml_add_to_info(parser,((char *) tag_name) + parser->toffset);

			add_assoc_string(tag,"tag",((char *) tag_name) + parser->toffset,1); /* cast to avoid gcc-warning */
			add_assoc_string(tag,"type","open",1);
			add_assoc_long(tag,"level",parser->level);
```

Crafted XML file

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Out-of-bounds write

- Supply this document to the vulnerable PHP XML parser.
- The parser's level counter increments beyond the array's capacity.
- An out-of-bounds write occurs at `parser->ltags[parser->level-1]`.
- This results in memory corruption.
- Subsequent memory operations may be hijacked for code execution.

[Mandatory] Fix code:
```c
		if (parser->data) {
			if (parser->level <= XML_MAXLEVEL)  {
```

commit_message:
Curl_urldecode: no peeking beyond end of input buffer

Security problem: CVE-2013-2174

If a program would give a string like "%FF" to curl_easy_unescape() but
ask for it to decode only the first byte, it would still parse and
decode the full hex sequence. The function then not only read beyond the
allowed buffer but it would also deduct the *unsigned* counter variable
for how many more bytes there's left to read in the buffer by two,
making the counter wrap. Continuing this, the function would go on
reading beyond the buffer and soon writing beyond the allocated target
buffer...

Bug: http://curl.haxx.se/docs/adv_20130622.html
Reported-by: Timo Sirainen

```c
#define MIN(a,b) ((a) < (b) ? (a) : (b))
```

commit_message:
ipv6: udp packets following an UFO enqueued packet need also be handled by UFO

In the following scenario the socket is corked:
If the first UDP packet is larger then the mtu we try to append it to the
write queue via ip6_ufo_append_data. A following packet, which is smaller
than the mtu would be appended to the already queued up gso-skb via
plain ip6_append_data. This causes random memory corruptions.

In ip6_ufo_append_data we also have to be careful to not queue up the
same skb multiple times. So setup the gso frame only when no first skb
is available.

This also fixes a shortcoming where we add the current packet's length to
cork->length but return early because of a packet > mtu with dontfrag set
(instead of sutracting it again).

Found with trinity.

```c
	else

}
```

fabio@192.168.1.100's password:

------------[ cut here ]------------
WARNING: at net/sched/sch_generic.c:255 dev_watchdog+0x2cc/0x2f0()

 r6:000000ff r5:80412388 r4:80685dc0 r3:80696cc0

CVE-2013-4511

[Mandatory] Title: CVE-2013-4511 / CWE-119:
Missing bounds check in uio_mmap_physical

[Optional] Disclosure / Patch Dates:
Initial advisory: 2013-11-12 — Patch release: Not available in input

[Optional] Affected products/versions:
Not available in input

The Vulnerability
[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:
CWE-119
[Mandatory] Summary:
The `uio_mmap_physical` function in `drivers/uio/uio.c` mapped physical memory for a user-space request without checking if the requested mapping size was within the bounds of the allocated memory region. This allowed a user to request a mapping larger than the specified `mem->size`, leading to an out-of-bounds memory mapping.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
The function `remap_pfn_range()` was called without first validating that `vma->vm_end - vma->vm_start` was less than or equal to `mem->size`.
[Mandatory] Attack Surface:
Local kernel driver interface (UIO)
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Local privilege escalation
[Optional] Trigger / Attack vector:
mmap() system call on a UIO device
[Mandatory] Key code/struct excerpt (minimal):
```c
static int uio_mmap_physical(struct vm_area_struct *vma)
{
	struct uio_device *idev = vma->vm_private_data;
	int mi = uio_find_mem_index(vma);
	if (mi < 0)
		return -EINVAL;

	vma->vm_ops = &uio_physical_vm_ops;
	vma->vm_page_prot = pgprot_noncached(vma->vm_page_prot);

	return remap_pfn_range(vma,
			       vma->vm_start,
			       idev->info->mem[mi].addr >> PAGE_SHIFT,
			       vma->vm_end - vma->vm_start,
			       vma->vm_page_prot);
}
```
Exploit:

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
mmap() system call on a UIO device file

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Arbitrary mapping of physical memory beyond intended region

[Mandatory] Exploitability summary (1 sentence):
A local user with access to the UIO device can trigger the vulnerability by requesting a memory map larger than the device's configured region, which is a straightforward operation.

[Mandatory] Exploit script (summary, 3—6 bullets):
- Open a UIO device file (e.g., `/dev/uio0`).
- Use `mmap()` to request a memory mapping with a length (`len`) larger than the size advertised for the memory region (e.g., via `/sys/class/uio/uio0/maps/map0/size`).
- The kernel will incorrectly map the requested length, potentially exposing or corrupting adjacent physical memory.
- This out-of-bounds mapping can be leveraged for local privilege escalation.

Fix
[Mandatory] Fix code:
```c
static int uio_mmap_physical(struct vm_area_struct *vma)
{
	struct uio_device *idev = vma->vm_private_data;
	int mi = uio_find_mem_index(vma);
	struct uio_mem *mem;
	if (mi < 0)
		return -EINVAL;
	mem = idev->info->mem + mi;

	if (vma->vm_end - vma->vm_start > mem->size)
		return -EINVAL;

	vma->vm_ops = &uio_physical_vm_ops;
	vma->vm_page_prot = pgprot_noncached(vma->vm_page_prot);

	/*
	 * We cannot use the vm_iomap_memory() helper here,
	 * because vma->vm_pgoff is the map index we looked
	 * up above in uio_find_mem_index(), rather than an
	 * actual page offset into the mmap.
	 *
	 * So we just do the physical mmap without a page
	 * offset.
	 */
	return remap_pfn_range(vma,
			       vma->vm_start,
			       mem->addr >> PAGE_SHIFT,
			       vma->vm_end - vma->vm_start,
			       vma->vm_page_prot);
}
```
[Mandatory] Fix summary:
The patch adds a check to ensure the requested mapping size (`vma->vm_end - vma->vm_start`) does not exceed the memory region's size (`mem->size`). If the check fails, the function returns `-EINVAL`.

[Optional] Patch reference:
https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/7314e613d5ff9f0934f7a0f74ed7973b903315d1
[Optional] Patch Analysis:
What did the fix do?
- Field: PatchType (bounds check added)
[Optional] Variant & Triage Guidance

[Optional] Variant analysis suggestions (2—3 bullets):
- Review other callers of `remap_pfn_range()` and `io_remap_pfn_range()` in the kernel for missing size checks.
- Fuzz the UIO subsystem, particularly the `mmap` handlers for different device types.
- Audit other kernel subsystems that perform physical memory mappings for similar issues.

[Optional] Likely variants/impact (one line):
Other kernel drivers performing memory mappings without proper size validation could be vulnerable to similar local privilege escalation flaws.

The Vulnerability
[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:
CWE-119 / CVE-2013-4511: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
[Mandatory] Summary:
A vulnerability exists in the `au1200fb_fb_mmap` function within `drivers/video/au1200fb.c`. The function fails to validate the user-provided mapping size and offset before calling `vm_iomap_memory`, as shown in the provided code excerpt. This allows a local attacker to map a memory region larger than the framebuffer, potentially leading to out-of-bounds access.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
The function `au1200fb_fb_mmap` lacks proper validation of the `vma->vm_end - vma->vm_start` range and `vma->vm_pgoff` offset before calling `vm_iomap_memory`.
[Mandatory] Attack Surface:
Kernel framebuffer driver
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Local privilege escalation
[Optional] Trigger / Attack vector:
mmap syscall on the au1200fb device file
[Mandatory] Key code/struct excerpt (minimal):

static int au1200fb_fb_mmap(struct fb_info *info, struct vm_area_struct *vma)
{
	struct au1200fb_device *fbdev = info->par;

	vma->vm_page_prot = pgprot_noncached(vma->vm_page_prot);
	pgprot_val(vma->vm_page_prot) |= _CACHE_MASK; /* CCA=7 */

	return vm_iomap_memory(vma, fbdev->fb_phys, fbdev->fb_len);
}

Exploit:

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
mmap syscall on the au1200fb device file

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Out-of-bounds memory mapping

[Mandatory] Exploitability summary (1 sentence):
An attacker with local access can control the mapping size and offset, making exploitation straightforward for achieving out-of-bounds memory access.

[Mandatory] Exploit script (summary, 3—6 bullets):
- Open the framebuffer device `/dev/fbX` associated with the `au1200fb` driver.
- Call `mmap()` on the device file descriptor.
- Specify a `length` in the `mmap` call that is larger than the actual framebuffer size (`fbdev->fb_len`).
- The kernel will map the requested larger region due to the missing bounds check.
- Access memory beyond the intended framebuffer boundaries through the returned mapping.

Fix
[Mandatory] Fix code:
if (vma->vm_pgoff > (~0UL >> PAGE_SHIFT)) {
	return -EINVAL;
}
...
if ((vma->vm_end - vma->vm_start + off) > len) {
	return -EINVAL;
}

[Mandatory] Fix summary:
The fix re-introduces bounds checks on the `vma->vm_pgoff` offset and the total requested mapping size (`vma->vm_end - vma->vm_start + off`) against the calculated framebuffer length (`len`), returning an error if the request is invalid.

https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/7314e613d5ff9f0934f7a0f74ed7973b903315d1

What did the fix do?
- Field: PatchType (e.g., bounds check added, logic refactor, feature removal)
bounds check added

- Review other framebuffer drivers (`drivers/video/`) for similar conversions to `vm_iomap_memory` that might have removed necessary checks.
- Audit other uses of `vm_iomap_memory` in the kernel to ensure they are always preceded by robust validation of offset and size parameters.
- Fuzz the `mmap` handlers of various drivers with large sizes and offsets to find similar regressions.

[Optional] Likely variants/impact (one line):
Similar out-of-bounds mapping vulnerabilities may exist in other drivers that underwent refactoring to use `vm_iomap_memory`.

[Mandatory] Title: CVE-2013-4512 / CWE-119:
Buffer overflow in exitcode_proc_write

[Optional] Disclosure / Patch Dates:
Initial advisory: 2013-11-12 — Patch release: Not available in input

[Optional] Affected products/versions:
Not available in input

The Vulnerability
[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:
CWE-119
[Mandatory] Summary:
The bug is in the `exitcode_proc_write` function within `arch/um/kernel/exitcode.c`. It is triggered when a user writes to the `/proc/exitcode` special file with a `count` larger than the size of the local `buf` array. The code is exploitable because it uses the user-provided `count` directly in a `copy_from_user` call without bounds checking, allowing a write past the end of the fixed-size stack buffer.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
Unchecked buffer length field from user input.
[Mandatory] Attack Surface:
proc filesystem write handler (local, requires root access)
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Local privilege escalation / Denial of Service
[Optional] Trigger / Attack vector:
Writing a string larger than 6 bytes to `/proc/exitcode`.
[Mandatory] Key code/struct excerpt (minimal):
static ssize_t exitcode_proc_write(struct file *file,
		const char __user *buffer, size_t count, loff_t *pos)
{
	char *end, buf[sizeof("nnnnn\0")];
	size_t size;
	int tmp;

	size = min(count, sizeof(buf));
	if (copy_from_user(buf, buffer, size))
		return -EFAULT;
Exploit:

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
proc filesystem write handler

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Stack-based buffer overflow (out-of-bounds write)

[Mandatory] Exploitability summary (1 sentence):
Exploitability is limited by requiring root access to write to the proc file, but a successful overflow can lead to local privilege escalation or kernel panic.

[Mandatory] Exploit script (summary, 3—6 bullets):
- An attacker with root privileges opens `/proc/exitcode` for writing.
- The attacker writes a string longer than 6 bytes (the size of `buf`).
- The `copy_from_user` call in the vulnerable version copies the entire input, overflowing the stack buffer `buf`.
- This overwrites adjacent stack data, potentially corrupting the return address or other critical variables.
- Controlled corruption can lead to arbitrary code execution in kernel context or a system crash.

Fix
[Mandatory] Fix code:
static ssize_t exitcode_proc_write(struct file *file,
		const char __user *buffer, size_t count, loff_t *pos)
{
	char *end, buf[sizeof("nnnnn\0")];
	size_t size;
	int tmp;

	size = min(count, sizeof(buf));
	if (copy_from_user(buf, buffer, size))
		return -EFAULT;

[Mandatory] Fix summary:
The patch adds a bounds check by limiting the size of data copied from the user to the size of the destination buffer, preventing a stack buffer overflow.

[Optional] Patch reference:
https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/201f99f170df14ba52ea4c52847779042b7a623b
[Optional] Patch Analysis:
What did the fix do?
- Field: PatchType (bounds check added)
[Optional] Variant & Triage Guidance

[Optional] Variant analysis suggestions (2—3 bullets):
- Review other `*_proc_write` handlers in the kernel for similar missing `min(count, sizeof(buf))` checks.
- Fuzz the proc filesystem interface, focusing on handlers that do not explicitly cap the `count` parameter.
- Audit code paths that use `copy_from_user` with a size derived directly from a user-provided value without validation.

[Optional] Likely variants/impact (one line):
Similar unchecked `copy_from_user` calls could lead to other local kernel memory corruption vulnerabilities.

[Mandatory] Title: CVE-2013-4514 / CWE-119:
Buffer overflow setting station name

[Optional] Disclosure / Patch Dates:
Initial advisory: 2013-11-12 — Patch release: Not available in input

[Optional] Affected products/versions:
Not available in input

The Vulnerability
[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:
Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer

[Mandatory] Summary:
In the `wvlan_uil_put_info` function within `drivers/staging/wlags49_h2/wl_priv.c`, the code copies a user-provided station name into a fixed-size kernel buffer without proper bounds checking. The vulnerability is triggered when a process with `CAP_NET_ADMIN` sends a request where the length field in the user data (`pLtv->u.u16[0]`) is larger than the destination buffer (`lp->StationName`). This leads to a heap-based buffer overflow, potentially corrupting adjacent kernel memory, making it exploitable.

[Mandatory] Root cause:
The code trusts the user-supplied length field `pLtv->u.u16[0]` and uses it directly in a `memcpy` operation into `lp->StationName`, without validating that it is within the bounds of the destination buffer.

[Mandatory] Attack Surface:
Kernel driver (wireless network driver)

[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Local privilege escalation

[Optional] Trigger / Attack vector:
Malicious IOCTL request from a privileged local process

[Mandatory] Key code/struct excerpt (minimal):
```c
case CFG_CNF_OWN_NAME:
    memset(lp->StationName, 0, sizeof(lp->StationName));
    memcpy((void *)lp->StationName, (void *)&pLtv->u.u8[2], (size_t)pLtv->u.u16[0]);
    pLtv->u.u16[0] = CNV_INT_TO_LITTLE(pLtv->u.u16[0]);
    break;
```

Exploit:

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
IOCTL from a process with CAP_NET_ADMIN

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Kernel heap out-of-bounds write

[Mandatory] Exploitability summary (1 sentence):
The exploit is straightforward for a local user with CAP_NET_ADMIN, as it only requires crafting an IOCTL with an oversized length field to corrupt kernel memory.

[Mandatory] Exploit script (summary, 3—6 bullets):
- Acquire a file descriptor to the vulnerable wireless device.
- Craft a `uilreq` structure where `data` points to a user buffer containing a `CFG_CNF_OWN_NAME` LTV record.
- In the LTV record, set the length field (`u.u16[0]`) to a value larger than `sizeof(lp->StationName)`.
- Include the station name data starting at `u.u8[2]` in the user buffer.
- Issue the IOCTL with the crafted request to trigger the buffer overflow in the kernel.

Fix
[Mandatory] Fix code:
```c
case CFG_CNF_OWN_NAME:
    memset(lp->StationName, 0, sizeof(lp->StationName));
    len = min_t(size_t, pLtv->u.u16[0], sizeof(lp->StationName));
    strlcpy(lp->StationName, &pLtv->u.u8[2], len);
    pLtv->u.u16[0] = CNV_INT_TO_LITTLE(pLtv->u.u16[0]);
    break;
```

[Mandatory] Fix summary:
The patch replaces the unsafe `memcpy` with `strlcpy` and introduces a `min_t` call to ensure the copy length does not exceed the size of the destination buffer, thus preventing the overflow.

[Optional] Patch reference:
Not available in input

- Field: PatchType (bounds check added, logic refactor)

[Optional] Variant & Triage Guidance

[Optional] Variant analysis suggestions (2—3 bullets):
- Review other `case` statements within the same `switch` block that perform `memcpy` or similar operations based on user-controlled lengths.
- Fuzz the driver's IOCTL handler with various malformed LTV records to uncover similar missing bounds checks.
- Audit the `CFG_ENCRYPT_STRING` case, which also uses `memcpy` with a user-controlled length (`pLtv->len`).

[Optional] Likely variants/impact (one line):
Other cases in the function may have similar unchecked `memcpy` calls leading to potential overflows.

[SVG] Resources should be laid out in dependecy order.

We're currently laying out resources in tree order, while they are
(conceptually) forming a DAG - and this disconnect results in
complicated logic and an extra layout pass attempting to re-validate
nodes that might have been invalidated by the resource layout. This is
broken in (at least) two ways:

  * two passes are not guaranteed to be enough, we could need an
    arbitrary number of passes to stabilize the tree.
  * the re-layout logic hangs off RenderSVGRoot, and falls apart when
    multiple root nodes are present (html doc with multiple svg fragments).

Recently introduced asserts are testing for render tree nodes which are
still marked for layout at paint time, and are catching several invariant
violations due to the above.

To address this problem, we should lay out resources in transitive
dependency order (where node A depends on resource B if it references
it directly: <rect id="a" filter="url(#b)"/>). Turns out this is not as
complicated as it sounds, and we can avoid building an explicit resources
DAG because we already have the sparse version: each node tracks the list
of resources it is referencing.

So before laying out a node, we should ensure that its resources are laid
out first. Applying this recursively, we are effectively traversing the
dependency DAG in the correct order.

(This relies on the assumption that a resource' layout does not depend on
its in-tree parent layout - which should be the case as resources only
make sense in the context of their clients).

The CL also removes the RenderSVGRoot re-layout logic added in
http://trac.webkit.org/changeset/111601 as it is no longer needed: a
resource is now guaranteed to be laid out before any of its clients.

Malicious HTML page

```cpp
void RenderView::layout()
{
    // ...
    for (RenderObject* child = firstChild(); child; child = child->nextSibling()) {
        if ((child->isBox() && toRenderBox(child)->hasRelativeLogicalHeight())
                || child->style()->logicalHeight().isPercent()
                || child->style()->logicalMinHeight().isPercent()
                || child->style()->logicalMaxHeight().isPercent()
                || child->style()->logicalHeight().isViewportPercentage()
                || child->style()->logicalMinHeight().isViewportPercentage()
                || child->style()->logicalMaxHeight().isViewportPercentage()
                || child->isSVGRoot())

        if (child->isSVGRoot()) {
            ASSERT(child->node());
            ASSERT(child->node()->isSVGElement());
            toSVGElement(child->node())->invalidateRelativeLengthClients(&layoutScope);
        }
    }
    // ...
}
```

commit_message:
[SVG] Resources should be laid out in dependecy order.

We're currently laying out resources in tree order, while they are
(conceptually) forming a DAG - and this disconnect results in
complicated logic and an extra layout pass attempting to re-validate
nodes that might have been invalidated by the resource layout. This is
broken in (at least) two ways:

  * two passes are not guaranteed to be enough, we could need an
    arbitrary number of passes to stabilize the tree.
  * the re-layout logic hangs off RenderSVGRoot, and falls apart when
    multiple root nodes are present (html doc with multiple svg fragments).

Recently introduced asserts are testing for render tree nodes which are
still marked for layout at paint time, and are catching several invariant
violations due to the above.

To address this problem, we should lay out resources in transitive
dependency order (where node A depends on resource B if it references
it directly: <rect id="a" filter="url(#b)"/>). Turns out this is not as
complicated as it sounds, and we can avoid building an explicit resources
DAG because we already have the sparse version: each node tracks the list
of resources it is referencing.

So before laying out a node, we should ensure that its resources are laid
out first. Applying this recursively, we are effectively traversing the
dependency DAG in the correct order.

(This relies on the assumption that a resource' layout does not depend on
its in-tree parent layout - which should be the case as resources only
make sense in the context of their clients).

The CL also removes the RenderSVGRoot re-layout logic added in
http://trac.webkit.org/changeset/111601 as it is no longer needed: a
resource is now guaranteed to be laid out before any of its clients.

```cpp
    if (read_buf_->offset() >= kMaxHeaderBufSize) {
      io_state_ = STATE_DONE;
      return ERR_RESPONSE_HEADERS_TOO_BIG;
```

Malicious HTTP response

    headers = new HttpResponseHeaders(HttpUtil::AssembleRawHeaders(
        read_buf_->StartOfBuffer() + read_buf_unused_offset_, end_offset));

The Vulnerability
[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:
Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
[Mandatory] Summary:
The bug exists in the `__nfs4_get_acl_uncached` function in `fs/nfs/nfs4proc.c`. When an ACL is fetched from the server and is not cached, the function copies the ACL data into a user-provided buffer without verifying if the buffer is large enough. This is triggered when a user calls `getxattr` on "system.nfs4_acl" with an undersized buffer, leading to an out-of-bounds write.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
The check for the user-provided buffer length (`buflen`) against the actual ACL length (`res.acl_len`) was missing before copying data.
[Mandatory] Attack Surface:
Network file system (NFSv4) client driver
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Local privilege escalation / Memory corruption
[Optional] Trigger / Attack vector:
`getxattr` system call on "system.nfs4_acl" for an NFSv4 mount
[Mandatory] Key code/struct excerpt (minimal):
```c
nfs4_write_cached_acl(inode, pages, res.acl_data_offset, res.acl_len);
if (buf)
	_copy_from_pages(buf, pages, res.acl_data_offset, res.acl_len);
```
Exploit:

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
`getxattr` system call on "system.nfs4_acl" for an NFSv4 mount

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Out-of-bounds write

- Call `getxattr` on a file on that mount, requesting the "system.nfs4_acl" attribute.

[Mandatory] Fix code:

```c
	if (res.acl_len > buflen) {

}
```
[Mandatory] Fix summary:
The patch adds a check to ensure that the length of the ACL data from the server (`res.acl_len`) does not exceed the size of the user-supplied buffer (`buflen`) before copying.

Commit 1f1ea6c "NFSv4: Fix buffer overflow checking in
__nfs4_get_acl_uncached" accidently dropped the checking for too small

```c
            for (; y < tile->comp[compno].coord[1][1] - s->image_offset_y; y += s->cdy[compno]) {
                uint8_t *dst;

                x   = tile->comp[compno].coord[0][0] - s->image_offset_x;
```

- Ensure the tile coordinates are set such that the calculated `x` and `y` values, when multiplied by `pixelsize` or `linesize`, result in an offset beyond the end of the picture buffer.

[Mandatory] Fix code:

commit_message:
wireless: radiotap: fix parsing buffer overrun

When parsing an invalid radiotap header, the parser can overrun
the buffer that is passed in because it doesn't correctly check
 1) the minimum radiotap header size
 2) the space for extended bitmaps

The first issue doesn't affect any in-kernel user as they all
check the minimum size before calling the radiotap function.
The second issue could potentially affect the kernel if an skb
is passed in that consists only of the radiotap header with a
lot of extended bitmaps that extend past the SKB. In that case
a read-only buffer overrun by at most 4 bytes is possible.

Fix this by adding the appropriate checks to the parser.

The vulnerability is in the `bdfReadCharacters` function within `src/bitmap/bdfread.c`. When parsing a BDF font file, the function uses `sscanf` with the `%s` format specifier to read a character name into the `charName` buffer without specifying a field width limit. This allows a specially crafted BDF file with a long character name to write past the 100-byte boundary of `charName`, causing a stack-based buffer overflow. The overflow is triggered by the `sscanf` call on the line reading the `STARTCHAR` keyword.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
The `sscanf` format string `%s` does not limit the number of characters written to the destination buffer `charName`.

    char        charName[100];

    if (sscanf((char *) line, "STARTCHAR %s", charName) != 1) {
        bdfError("bad character name in BDF file\n");
        goto BAILOUT;    /* bottom of function, free and return error */
    }

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
File parsing via a malicious BDF font file.

- Control of the overflowed data can lead to arbitrary code execution when the function returns.

    int         ignore;

commit_message:
Fix crash in WebContentsViewAura::WindowObserver that happens when switching tabs. The exact repro steps were:

1) open an empty page
2) print preview
3) open a new tab
4) go back to original tab
5) close print preview
6) switch to the new tab

The crash happened at step 4 because the second tab got removed from the same root window as the print preview's observer. We weren't unobserving all the children of the root window at that point.

commit_message:
Kill worker process by way of a sync IPC message before it cleans up.

When a worker process shuts down, it shuts down WebKit. If there are
other threads running in the worker process, this leads to crashes.
This fix tries to kill the worker process forcibly so that no cleanup
takes place.

commit_message:
cifs: ensure that uncached writes handle unmapped areas correctly

It's possible for userland to pass down an iovec via writev() that has a
bogus user pointer in it. If that happens and we're doing an uncached
write, then we can end up getting less bytes than we expect from the
call to iov_iter_copy_from_user. This is CVE-2014-0069

cifs_iovec_write isn't set up to handle that situation however. It'll
blindly keep chugging through the page array and not filling those pages
with anything useful. Worse yet, we'll later end up with a negative
number in wdata->tailsz, which will confuse the sending routines and
cause an oops at the very least.

Fix this by having the copy phase of cifs_iovec_write stop copying data
in this situation and send the last write as a short one. At the same
time, we want to avoid sending a zero-length write to the server, so
break out of the loop and set rc to -EFAULT if that happens. This also
allows us to handle the case where no address in the iovec is valid.

[Note: Marking this for stable on v3.4+ kernels, but kernels as old as
       v2.6.38 may have a similar problem and may need similar fix]

commit_message:
Bug 694957: fix stack buffer overflow in xps_parse_color

xps_parse_color happily reads more than FZ_MAX_COLORS values out of a
ContextColor array which overflows the passed in samples array.
Limiting the number of allowed samples to FZ_MAX_COLORS and make sure
to use that constant for all callers fixes the problem.

Thanks to Jean-Jamil Khalifé for reporting and investigating the issue
and providing a sample exploit file.

commit_message:
kvm: x86: fix emulator buffer overflow (CVE-2014-0049)

The problem occurs when the guest performs a pusha with the stack
address pointing to an mmio address (or an invalid guest physical
address) to start with, but then extending into an ordinary guest
physical address.  When doing repeated emulated pushes
emulator_read_write sets mmio_needed to 1 on the first one.  On a
later push when the stack points to regular memory,
mmio_nr_fragments is set to 0, but mmio_is_needed is not set to 0.

As a result, KVM exits to userspace, and then returns to
complete_emulated_mmio.  In complete_emulated_mmio
vcpu->mmio_cur_fragment is incremented.  The termination condition of
vcpu->mmio_cur_fragment == vcpu->mmio_nr_fragments is never achieved.
The code bounces back and fourth to userspace incrementing
mmio_cur_fragment past it's buffer.  If the guest does nothing else it
eventually leads to a a crash on a memcpy from invalid memory address.

However if a guest code can cause the vm to be destroyed in another
vcpu with excellent timing, then kvm_clear_async_pf_completion_queue
can be used by the guest to control the data that's pointed to by the
call to cancel_work_item, which can be used to gain execution.

The Vulnerability
[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:

[Mandatory] Summary:
The `ip6_route_add` function in the IPv6 routing code incorrectly passes the `DST_NOCOUNT` flag to `ip6_dst_alloc` for all new routes. This flag bypasses reference counting, allowing an attacker to add an unlimited number of routes via router advertisements without being limited by the kernel's memory accounting, leading to potential memory exhaustion.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
The `DST_NOCOUNT` flag is unconditionally passed to `ip6_dst_alloc`, bypassing accounting checks for routes added remotely.

Network stack (IPv6 router advertisement handling)
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Remote Denial of Service (memory exhaustion)

Malicious IPv6 router advertisement messages

	rt = ip6_dst_alloc(net, NULL, DST_NOCOUNT, table);

IPv6 router advertisements

Unbounded kernel memory allocation

- Each advertisement triggers the `ip6_route_add` function in the kernel.
- The function calls `ip6_dst_alloc` with the `DST_NOCOUNT` flag.

[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:
CWE-119: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
[Mandatory] Summary:
The bug is in the mget function in src/softmagic.c, where multiple manual boundary checks (e.g., `if (nbytes < offset || nbytes < (offset + size))`) fail to correctly prevent integer overflow when calculating `offset + size`. An attacker can trigger this by providing a crafted file that causes a large offset value, leading to an out-of-bounds read or write. The flaw is exploitable because the insufficient checks allow the offset calculation to wrap, bypassing the intended bounds validation and accessing memory beyond the input buffer.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
Incomplete boundary checks that do not prevent integer overflow in offset calculations.

File parsing via the file command utility.
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Out-of-bounds read/write leading to potential information disclosure or denial of service.
[Optional] Trigger / Attack vector:
Crafted file processed by the file utility.
[Mandatory] Key code/struct excerpt (minimal):

```c
case FILE_BELONG:
case FILE_BEID3:
    if (nbytes < offset || nbytes < (offset + 4))
        return 0;
    if (off) {
        switch (m->in_op & FILE_OPS_MASK) {
        case FILE_OPAND:
            offset = (int32_t)((p->hl[0]<<24)|
                     (p->hl[1]<<16)|
                     (p->hl[2]<<8)|
                     (p->hl[3])) &
                     off;
            break;
```

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
Crafted file input to the file utility.

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Out-of-bounds read, potential out-of-bounds write.

Exploitable by supplying a file with a large offset field that causes integer overflow in boundary checks, leading to memory access violations.

- Ensure the offset plus size calculation overflows a 32-bit integer.

[Mandatory] Fix code:

```c
case FILE_BELONG:
case FILE_BEID3:
    if (OFFSET_OOB(nbytes, offset, 4))
        return 0;
    if (off) {
        switch (m->in_op & FILE_OPS_MASK) {
        case FILE_OPAND:
            offset = (int32_t)((p->hl[0]<<24)|
                     (p->hl[1]<<16)|
                     (p->hl[2]<<8)|
                     (p->hl[3])) &
                     off;
            break;
```
[Mandatory] Fix summary:
Replaced manual boundary checks with the OFFSET_OOB macro to correctly handle integer overflow and ensure robust validation.

commit_message:
skbuff: skb_segment: orphan frags before copying

skb_segment copies frags around, so we need
to copy them carefully to avoid accessing
user memory after reporting completion to userspace
through a callback.

skb_segment doesn't normally happen on datapath:
TSO needs to be disabled - so disabling zero copy
in this case does not look like a big deal.

[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:

The vulnerability exists in the `scsi_init_iovec` function within `hw/scsi-disk.c`. The function calculates the I/O vector length using `r->iov.iov_len = MIN(r->sector_count * 512, SCSI_DMA_BUF_SIZE)`. However, the `r->buflen` field, which determines the actual allocated buffer size, is not initialized if `r->iov.iov_base` is already set, leading to a potential mismatch between the calculated length and the allocated buffer size. SCSI disk emulation in QEMU
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Local privilege escalation

Malicious SCSI request from a guest OS

static uint32_t scsi_init_iovec(SCSIDiskReq *r)
{
    SCSIDiskState *s = DO_UPCAST(SCSIDiskState, qdev, r->req.dev);

    if (!r->iov.iov_base) {
        r->buflen = SCSI_DMA_BUF_SIZE;
        r->iov.iov_base = qemu_blockalign(s->bs, r->buflen);
    }
    r->iov.iov_len = MIN(r->sector_count * 512, r->buflen);
    qemu_iovec_init_external(&r->qiov, &r->iov, 1);
    return r->qiov.size / 512;
}

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
SCSI disk request handling

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Buffer overflow write

- The `scsi_init_iovec` function is called, and `r->iov.iov_len` is calculated based on the uninitialized `r->buflen`.

- The memory corruption can be leveraged to escape the guest VM and achieve code execution on the host.

[Mandatory] Fix code:
static uint32_t scsi_init_iovec(SCSIDiskReq *r)
{
    SCSIDiskState *s = DO_UPCAST(SCSIDiskState, qdev, r->req.dev);

    if (!r->iov.iov_base) {
        r->buflen = SCSI_DMA_BUF_SIZE;
        r->iov.iov_base = qemu_blockalign(s->bs, r->buflen);
    }
    r->iov.iov_len = MIN(r->sector_count * 512, r->buflen);
    qemu_iovec_init_external(&r->qiov, &r->iov, 1);
    return r->qiov.size / 512;
}

The patch ensures that `r->buflen` is correctly initialized to `SCSI_DMA_BUF_SIZE` before it is used to calculate the I/O vector length, preventing the buffer overflow.

- A guest VM prepares a sequence of SCSI read/write commands.
- The guest sends these commands to the emulated SCSI disk controller.
- For each command, the QEMU `scsi_new_request` function is called.

[Mandatory] Fix code:
```c
static SCSIRequest *scsi_new_request(SCSIDevice *d, uint32_t tag,
                                     uint32_t lun, void *hba_private)
{

    SCSIRequest *req;

    req = scsi_req_alloc(&scsi_disk_reqops, &s->qdev, tag, lun, hba_private);
    return req;
}
```

[Mandatory] Fix summary:
The patch removes the unconditional allocation of the bounce buffer, making it lazy. The buffer is now only allocated when explicitly needed, preventing excessive memory consumption for requests that do not require it.

- Field: PatchType (logic refactor)

flask: fix reading strings from guest memory

Since the string size is being specified by the guest, we must range
check it properly before doing allocations based on it. While for the
two cases that are exposed only to trusted guests (via policy
restriction) this just uses an arbitrary upper limit (PAGE_SIZE), for
the FLASK_[GS]ETBOOL case (which any guest can use) the upper limit
gets enforced based on the longest name across all boolean settings.

This is XSA-84.

commit_message:
vhost: fix total length when packets are too short

When mergeable buffers are disabled, and the
incoming packet is too large for the rx buffer,
get_rx_bufs returns success.

This was intentional in order for make recvmsg
truncate the packet and then handle_rx would
detect err != sock_len and drop it.

Unfortunately we pass the original sock_len to
recvmsg - which means we use parts of iov not fully
validated.

Fix this up by detecting this overrun and doing packet drop
immediately.

commit_message:
tools: arm: remove code to check for a DTB appended to the kernel

The code to check for an appended DTB was confusing and unnecessary. Since we
know the size of the kernel binary passed to us we should just load the entire
thing into guest RAM (subject to the limits checks). Removing this code avoids
a whole raft of overflow and alignment issues.

We also need to validate the limits of the segment where we intend to load the
kernel to avoid overflow issues.

For ARM32 we control the load address, but we need to validate the size. The
entry point is only relevant within the guest so we don't need to worry about
that.

For ARM64 we need to validate both the load address (which is the same as the
entry point) and the size.

This is XSA-95.

```cpp
  // Allocate a shared memory buffer to hold the bitmap bits.
  shared_buf_.reset(ChildThread::current()->AllocateSharedMemory(buf_size));
  if (!shared_buf_)
    return;

  // Copy the bits into shared memory
  DCHECK(shared_buf_->memory());
  memcpy(shared_buf_->memory(), pixels, buf_size);
```

commit_message:
ALSA: control: Fix replacing user controls

There are two issues with the current implementation for replacing user
controls. The first is that the code does not check if the control is actually a
user control and neither does it check if the control is owned by the process
that tries to remove it. That allows userspace applications to remove arbitrary
controls, which can cause a user after free if a for example a driver does not
expect a control to be removed from under its feed.

The second issue is that on one hand when a control is replaced the
user_ctl_count limit is not checked and on the other hand the user_ctl_count is
increased (even though the number of user controls does not change). This allows
userspace, once the user_ctl_count limit as been reached, to repeatedly replace
a control until user_ctl_count overflows. Once that happens new controls can be
added effectively bypassing the user_ctl_count limit.

Both issues can be fixed by instead of open-coding the removal of the control
that is to be replaced to use snd_ctl_remove_user_ctl(). This function does
proper permission checks as well as decrements user_ctl_count after the control
has been removed.

Note that by using snd_ctl_remove_user_ctl() the check which returns -EBUSY at
beginning of the function if the control already exists is removed. This is not
a problem though since the check is quite useless, because the lock that is
protecting the control list is released between the check and before adding the
new control to the list, which means that it is possible that a different
control with the same settings is added to the list after the check. Luckily
there is another check that is done while holding the lock in snd_ctl_add(), so
we'll rely on that to make sure that the same control is not added twice.

```c
	size_t ss = CDF_SHORT_SEC_SIZE(h);
```

```c
	size_t ss = CDF_SHORT_SEC_SIZE(h);
```

The Vulnerability

The vulnerability exists in the `mconvert` function within `ext/fileinfo/libmagic/softmagic.c` when handling `FILE_PSTRING` types. The function calculates the string length from the input and copies data into a fixed-size buffer `p->s`. If the reported length is greater than or equal to the buffer size, the code attempts to truncate it to `sizeof(p->s) - 1`, which fails to account for the size of the length prefix itself (`sz`), potentially allowing a buffer overflow during the subsequent `while` loop copy.

[Mandatory] Root cause:
The truncation logic for a Pascal string length does not subtract the size of the length prefix, leading to an out-of-bounds write.

[Mandatory] Attack Surface:
File processing library (libmagic)

[Mandatory] Impact Summary:

	case FILE_PSTRING: {
		char *ptr1 = p->s, *ptr2 = ptr1 + file_pstring_length_size(m);
		size_t len = file_pstring_get_length(m, ptr1);
		if (len >= sizeof(p->s))
			len = sizeof(p->s) - 1;
		while (len--)
			*ptr1++ = *ptr2++;
		*ptr1 = '\0';
		return 1;
	}

File parsing via the libmagic library

- Set the Pascal string length field to a value greater than the destination buffer size.

- When the file is processed by a vulnerable version of `libmagic`, the `mconvert` function will overflow the `p->s` buffer.

Fix
[Mandatory] Fix code:
	case FILE_PSTRING: {
		size_t sz = file_pstring_length_size(m);
		char *ptr1 = p->s, *ptr2 = ptr1 + sz;
		size_t len = file_pstring_get_length(m, ptr1);
		if (len >= sizeof(p->s)) {
			/*
			 * The size of the pascal string length (sz)
			 * is 1, 2, or 4. We need at least 1 byte for NUL
			 * termination, but we've already truncated the
			 * string by p->s, so we need to deduct sz.
			 */ 
			len = sizeof(p->s) - sz;
		}
		while (len--)
			*ptr1++ = *ptr2++;
		*ptr1 = '\0';
		return 1;
	}

[Mandatory] Title: CVE-2014-3478 / CWE-119:

The Vulnerability
[Optional] CWE/CVE Number and description:
CWE-119
[Mandatory] Summary:
The bug is in the `mconvert` function when handling a `FILE_PSTRING` type. It calculates the length of a Pascal string and copies it into a fixed-size buffer `p->s`. If the length is too large, the code attempts to truncate it, but the calculation for the new length is incorrect, leading to a potential buffer overflow during the copy operation.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
Incorrect calculation of the truncated length for a Pascal string, leading to an out-of-bounds write.
[Mandatory] Attack Surface:
File parsing utility
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:
Denial of Service
[Optional] Trigger / Attack vector:
Specially crafted file
[Mandatory] Key code/struct excerpt (minimal):

```c
case FILE_PSTRING: {
    char *ptr1 = p->s, *ptr2 = ptr1 + file_pstring_length_size(m);
    size_t len = file_pstring_get_length(m, ptr1);
    if (len >= sizeof(p->s))
        len = sizeof(p->s) - 1;
    while (len--)
        *ptr1++ = *ptr2++;
    *ptr1 = '\0';
    return 1;
}
```

Exploit:

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
File parsing

[Mandatory] Exploit primitive(s) available:
Stack-based buffer overflow

[Mandatory] Exploitability summary (1 sentence):
An attacker can trigger this vulnerability by providing a file with a Pascal string where the length field specifies a size larger than the destination buffer, leading to an out-of-bounds write.

[Mandatory] Exploit script (summary, 3—6 bullets):
- Create a file with a magic entry that triggers the `FILE_PSTRING` case in `mconvert`.
- Craft the Pascal string length field to be a value larger than `sizeof(p->s)`.
- Ensure the string data following the length field is present.
- When the `file` utility processes the crafted file, the `mconvert` function will be called.
- The flawed truncation logic will cause the `while` loop to write past the end of the `p->s` buffer.
- This results in a denial of service or potentially arbitrary code execution.

Fix
[Mandatory] Fix code:
```c
case FILE_PSTRING: {
    size_t sz = file_pstring_length_size(m);
    char *ptr1 = p->s, *ptr2 = ptr1 + sz;
    size_t len = file_pstring_get_length(m, ptr1);
    if (len >= sizeof(p->s)) {
        /*
         * The size of the pascal string length (sz)
         * is 1, 2, or 4. We need at least 1 byte for NUL
         * termination, but we've already truncated the
         * string by p->s, so we need to deduct sz.
         */ 
        len = sizeof(p->s) - sz;
    }
    while (len--)
        *ptr1++ = *ptr2++;
    *ptr1 = '\0';
    return 1;
}
```

[Mandatory] Fix summary:
The patch correctly computes the truncated string size by subtracting the size of the length field (`sz`) from the total buffer size, ensuring the copy operation does not overflow the destination buffer.

```c
            VIM_CLEAR(eval_result[nested]);
        }
    }
```

Regular expression substitution with expression evaluation.

The Vulnerability

Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
[Mandatory] Summary:
The vulnerability exists in the `map_vcpu_info` function within `xen/common/domain.c`. A guest can register any guest physical address for the `vcpu_info` structure, provided it fits within the page frame, without the hypervisor verifying its alignment. This could lead to a fatal data abort on architectures like Arm 32-bit (which forbids all unaligned accesses) and Arm 64-bit (which forbids unaligned atomic accesses), potentially causing a denial of service for the guest.
[Mandatory] Root cause:
The function did not validate the alignment of the provided `offset` against the natural alignment requirements of the `vcpu_info_t` structure.

Hypervisor guest management interface (VCPUOP_register_vcpu_info)
[Mandatory] Impact Summary:

[Optional] Trigger / Attack vector:
VCPU operation request from a guest to register a vcpu_info structure at an unaligned address.
[Mandatory] Key code/struct excerpt (minimal):
```c
int map_vcpu_info(struct vcpu *v, unsigned long gfn, unsigned offset)
{
    struct domain *d = v->domain;
    void *mapping;
    vcpu_info_t *new_info;
    struct page_info *page;
    unsigned int align;

    if ( offset > (PAGE_SIZE - sizeof(vcpu_info_t)) )
        return -EINVAL;

#ifdef CONFIG_COMPAT
    if ( has_32bit_shinfo(d) )
        align = alignof(new_info->compat);
    else
#endif
        align = alignof(*new_info);
    if ( offset & (align - 1) )
```

- The hypervisor's `map_vcpu_info` function processes the request.

```c

    if ( offset > (PAGE_SIZE - sizeof(vcpu_info_t)) )
        return -EINVAL;

#ifdef CONFIG_COMPAT
    if ( has_32bit_shinfo(d) )

    else
#endif
        align = alignof(*new_info);
    if ( offset & (align - 1) )
```

commit_message:
xen: Check the alignment of the offset pased via VCPUOP_register_vcpu_info

Currently a guest is able to register any guest physical address to use
for the vcpu_info structure as long as the structure can fits in the
rest of the frame.

This means a guest can provide an address that is not aligned to the
natural alignment of the structure.

On Arm 32-bit, unaligned access are completely forbidden by the
hypervisor. This will result to a data abort which is fatal.

On Arm 64-bit, unaligned access are only forbidden when used for atomic
access. As the structure contains fields (such as evtchn_pending_self)
that are updated using atomic operations, any unaligned access will be
fatal as well.

While the misalignment is only fatal on Arm, a generic check is added
as an x86 guest shouldn't sensibly pass an unaligned address (this
would result to a split lock).

This is XSA-327.

The function calculates the size using integer division, which truncates the result for inputs not divisible by 4, causing a buffer to be allocated that is too small. This can trigger a buffer overflow when decoding Base64 data.

 The required result buffer size is underestimated due to integer division that does not account for padding.

static inline size_t base64_estimate_decode_size(size_t base64_in_size)

    return ((base64_in_size / 4) * 3);
}

[Mandatory] Trigger surface/attack vector:
API call to Base64 decoder with a specially crafted input string.

A buffer overflow exists in the `xgmac_enet_send` function in `hw/net/xgmac.c`. The function aggregates data from multiple network descriptors into a fixed-size stack buffer (`frame[8192]`). Due to missing break statements after error checks and an incorrect overflow check, the total size of the data being copied can exceed the buffer's capacity, leading to an out-of-bounds write.

The function accumulates data from multiple descriptors without properly breaking out of the processing loop on malformed descriptor conditions and fails to correctly check the cumulative size against the destination buffer.

```c
        len = (bd.buffer1_size & 0xfff) + (bd.buffer2_size & 0xfff);
```
